Getting Started with {poscosea}

Ph.D. Ohkubo Yusaku

2026-11-11

Source: vignettes/getting-started.Rmd
getting-started.Rmd
library(poscosea)

Overview

poscosea provides fast sensitivity analysis for posterior summaries obtained from MCMC output. The package implements infinitesimal jackknife (IJK) approximations based on

  • posterior draws of a scalar quantity of interest,
  • corresponding log-likelihood draws.

These influence values can then be used for

  • nonparametric bootstrap approximations,
  • leave-k-out cross-validation,
  • sensitivity analysis without refitting the original Bayesian model.

Installation

This package is available on GitHub.

You can install it using remotes:

install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("OhkuboYusaku/poscosea")

Or using devtools:

install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("OhkuboYusaku/poscosea")

Input Format

The main function requires

  • a numeric vector of posterior draws (theta)
  • a log-likelihood matrix (loglik)

Rows of loglik correspond to the posterior draws in theta and columns correspond to observations.

set.seed(123)
n_obs <- 6
y <- rnorm(n_obs, sd = 1)
# Introduce two influential observations.
signal_idx <- c(2, 5)
y[signal_idx] <- y[signal_idx] + 3

# Under y_i | theta ~ N(theta, 1) and a flat prior on theta,
# theta | y is Normal(mean(y), 1 / n_obs).
n_draws <- 2000
theta <- rnorm(n_draws, mean = mean(y), sd = 1 / sqrt(n_obs))

# Pointwise log-likelihood evaluated at the corresponding posterior draws.
loglik <- matrix(0, n_draws, n_obs)
for (i in seq_len(n_obs)) {
  loglik[, i] <- dnorm(y[i], mean = theta, sd = 1, log = TRUE)
}

Constructing an IJK Object

The ijk() function computes the posterior mean and observation-wise influence values.

fit <- ijk(theta, loglik)

The estimated posterior mean is stored in

fit$estimate
#> [1] 1.458558

The observation-wise influence values are stored in

head(fit$influence)
#> [1] -0.33446200  0.22035093  0.01858467 -0.22934285  0.28023625  0.04463300

Bootstrap Approximation

Bootstrap replicates can be generated from the influence values.

boot <- ijk_bootstrap(
  estimate = fit$estimate,
  influence = fit$influence,
  B = 500
)

Summary statistics can be obtained from the bootstrap distribution.

print(boot)
#> 
#> IJK Bootstrap Summary
#> 
#> Original estimate: 1.459 
#> 
#> Bootstrap replicates: 500 
#> 
#> Bias: -0.003 
#> Bootstrap SE: 0.521 
#> 95% percentile interval:
#> [0.455, 2.481]

Leave-One-Out Approximation

Leave-one-out approximations are obtained by setting k = 1.

loo <- ijk_lko(
  estimate = fit$estimate,
  influence = fit$influence,
  k = 1
)

The influence values can be visualized with plot(). For leave-one-out (k = 1), each point shows the approximate change in the estimate when one observation is removed. Large absolute values indicate highly influential observations.

plot(loo)

Leave-k-Out Approximation

More generally, k can be any integer from 1 to the number of observations, provided the number of omission sets does not exceed 1e6.

lko <- ijk_lko(
  estimate = fit$estimate,
  influence = fit$influence,
  k = 2
)

Plotting for k > 1

The current plot.ijk_lko() method is available only for k = 1. For k > 1, the object contains all leave-k-out estimates in lko$lko_estimates; inspect them directly or summarize them with summary(lko$lko_estimates).

N-Mixture Models

For hierarchical count data analysed with a binomial N-mixture model, see vignette("nmix-twostage", package = "poscosea"), which describes the two-stage (site and visit) bootstrap approximation implemented in nmix_loglik(), ijk_nmix() and ijk_bootstrap_2stage().
